description:
Enum.uniq_by (lib/enum.fz uniq_walk) keeps the keys it has seen in a list and scans it with List.member? for every element, so n elements with d distinct keys cost n*d comparisons. Elixir's Enum.uniq keeps them in a map. In the distiller (Enum.uniq over every job label) this scan is 37% of the 32,000-line run on PR #585: fz_op_identical 1240 of 3385 samples, 752 directly from the one compiled function.
Change: uniq_walk carries a map of seen keys (Map.has_key? / Map.put). Order of the result and === semantics are unchanged (map keys are strict: 1 and 1.0 are different keys).
Measured with the change on #585, tools/distill-telemetry.exs unchanged: 32,000 lines 2.90 s -> 1.56 s user; full 222,411-line log 19.9 s -> 13.7 s; output byte-identical to Elixir on both.
Signal: a fixture runs Enum.uniq over many distinct binaries on interp, run and build against an Elixir oracle, and pins the allocation count so the cost is linear in the input.
title: Enum.uniq and uniq_by remember what they have seen in a map
